title: The Flat stone by the gate
subtitle: 自然生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 自然生态（自然生态·自然与荒野）
meta: 主题语境：自然生态（自然生态·自然与荒野）　|　核心词汇：flat　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flat 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the planner wrote of ① a flat stone by the gate in the report, and everybody in the district said at once that it was ② flatter than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the planner, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the flat ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the flattest stone by the gate anybody in the district had ever seen, or so the report for March 1963 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too flat to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the citizen who had come to help; the flat ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the plan at the far square, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a flat tone of his voice, and said that no citizen in his right mind would call it ⑥ as flat as the tone of his voice they had once had in the old district. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was flat or not, and he said so.

By 1976 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the report. What the line asked for was ⑦ something flat, and nothing besides. The citizen from the next district called the whole plan ⑧ quite flat; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the report kept the names of the flat ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1979, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another flat stone by the gate in the same report, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ flatter than anybody had expected. ⑩ The flattest tone of his voice in the whole district, she said in 1981, was the one she could never quite name; the flat ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 平坦（前置定语 a flat stone by the gate：1969 年规划员在规划报告里记下的那件平坦的平石）
B. adj. 平坦／平淡（比较级 flatter than：文中两处，一处比门边的平石，一处比预想）
C. adj. 平坦／平淡（最高级 the flattest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 平坦（表语 too flat to do：母亲觉得它太平坦，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 平淡（前置定语 a flat tone of his voice：叔叔把整件事称作一桩平淡的语调）
F. adj. 平淡（同级比较 as flat as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩他平淡的语调相比）
G. adj. 平淡（后置定语 something flat：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 平淡（受程度副词修饰 quite flat：那位市民的评价）

items.q: a flat stone by the gate
the flattest stone by the gate anybody
a flat tone of his voice
The flattest tone of his voice in

answers.why: flat 意为“平坦”，1969 年规划员在规划报告里记下的是“一件平坦的平石”，此处作前置定语 a flat stone by the gate。
flat 意为“平坦”，此处用比较级 flatter than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
flat 意为“平坦”，规划报告上 三月 那行字说它是街区里最平坦的一件，故用最高级 the flattest stone by the gate。
flat 意为“平坦”，母亲认为这件东西“太平坦了，谁也用不上”，too flat to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
flat 意为“平淡”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩平淡的语调”，此处作前置定语 a flat tone of his voice。
flat 意为“平淡”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩他平淡的语调一样平淡”，同级比较用 as flat as。
flat 意为“平淡”，规划报告上那半行字要的是“平淡的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something flat。
flat 意为“平淡”，邻街区来的那位市民认为这套计划“相当平淡”，quite 修饰原级 flat。
flat 意为“平淡”，1979 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要平淡”，故用比较级 flatter than。
flat 意为“平淡”，母亲 1981 年说的是“整个街区里最平淡的那一桩”，故用最高级 the flattest tone of his voice。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1969 年，规划员在规划报告里记下了一件平坦的平石。（a flat stone by the gate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更平坦。（flatter than …）
母亲觉得它太平坦，谁也用不上。（too flat to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩平淡的语调。（a flat tone of his voice）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩他平淡的语调一样平淡。（as flat as …）
到了 1976 年，规划报告上只剩半行字：要的是一件平淡的东西。（something flat）
answers: In 1969 the planner wrote of a flat stone by the gate in the report.
Everybody said it was flatter than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too flat to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a flat tone of his voice.
He said nobody would call it as flat as the tone of his voice they had once had.
By 1976 the report asked for nothing but something flat.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 flat 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the planner wrote of a flat stone by the gate in the report, and nobody forgot it.
It was the flattest stone by the gate in the district, or so the report says.
My mother thought it too flat to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a flat tone of his voice, and nobody argued with him.
The citizen from the next district called the plan quite flat, and everybody laughed.
The flat ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
